family.description: This family represents MagC and related proteins that adopt an NlpC/P60-like fold but are catalytically inactive [[cite:PUB00164055]]. The structure consists of a six-stranded beta-sheet and five alpha-helices with a Cys-His-His catalytic triad characteristic of NlpC/P60 peptidases. However, a conserved tryptophan residue distorts the active site conformation, rendering these proteins unable to cleave peptidoglycan while retaining the ability to bind it [[cite:PUB00164055]]. In Pseudomonas aeruginosa, MagC is part of a type II alpha-2- macroglobulin complex encoded by the magABCDEF operon, where it directly interacts with the macroglobulin MagD [[cite:PUB00164055]]. These proteins are proposed to anchor the macroglobulin complex to the peptidoglycan layer in the bacterial periplasm [[cite:PUB00164055]].
family.name: MagC peptidoglycan-binding NlpC/P60-like protein
